turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: Good morning, this is The Morning Commute. Friday, October 9th. I'm Sam.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: And I'm Alex. Witnesses have put Eritrean soldiers on the wrong side of a border in northern Ethiopia, and that changes what the fighting in Tigray is.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: Reuters reports that witnesses saw 2 trucks carrying dozens of Eritrean soldiers in Adigrat, in Ethiopia's Tigray region, and a local official told AFP the troops had been there for days. Fighting between the TPLF and Ethiopian federal forces began on September 23.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: Reuters says this would be the first confirmation of Eritrean troops on Ethiopian soil in this conflict. Eritrea's information minister denies it and calls the claim a pretext for a war of aggression. Ethiopia had not commented. A Tigray Peace Force commander claims heavy weapons are involved too, but Reuters has not verified that.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: The reason it matters is history. Eritrean forces were central to the 2020 to 2022 war, and any return would pull a second state back into a conflict that was supposed to be settled by the Pretoria agreement. A denial plus photographic witnesses is the standard opening of a regional escalation, not the end of one.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: To Europe, where there is a quieter diplomatic story. Chancellor Merz received British Prime Minister Andy Burnham in Berlin on Thursday, Burnham's first visit since taking office on July 20, and the 2 governments exchanged ratification documents for the German-UK friendship treaty, known as the Kensington Treaty.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: Ratification is the unglamorous part that makes a treaty real. For a British government trying to rebuild its European relationships, doing it in the first months, at the chancellery, is a signal about where the new prime minister wants his weight to sit.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: And on Iran, Brent has pulled back after Donald Trump said productive discussions are under way with Tehran. AP has Brent down about 1% this morning to roughly $103 a barrel, after a 4.1% jump on Thursday on the back of the Gulf shipping attacks.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: So a one-line comment from the President is moving a market that had been pricing a war. We have seen this loop several times now. Talks are announced, oil sags, then another tanker is hit and it all reverses.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: The AI trade had its worst day in almost 2 months. The Financial Times reports OpenAI's annualized revenue is closer to $50 billion at the end of September, against the $68 billion to $70 billion figure that circulated in late September. CNBC reports the higher number had included partners' gross revenue.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: The market reaction was immediate. The Nasdaq fell 1.25%, its biggest one-day drop since mid-August. Oracle lost 5.5%, Broadcom 4.3%, Micron 4.8% and Nvidia 2.9%.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: What makes it more than a revenue-definition squabble is the financing. The Wall Street Journal reports Broadcom is lining up $50 billion of financing for OpenAI, and Oracle is also seeking money. Once the customer's revenue is smaller than the story, the question moves to who is holding the debt.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: The distinction between net and gross revenue is exactly how circular deals get flattered, and it is why credit desks, not equity desks, will drive the next leg of this story.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: The deal tape. Semafor reported on October 6 that Chipotle, with a market value of roughly $39 billion to $40 billion, has tapped bankers to fend off a takeover. Starbucks is Semafor's own theory and no bid has been received.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: On Thursday, Viatris agreed to buy Pacira at $36.50 a share, about $1.65 billion, and Crescent Energy agreed to buy Devon's Eagle Ford assets for about $3.85 billion. Mid-size deals are getting done even when the AI trade wobbles.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: In consumer staples, PepsiCo beat in its third quarter. Adjusted earnings per share were $2.34 against $2.29 expected, and revenue was $25.27 billion, up 5.6%, ahead of roughly $25.0 billion expected. Operating profit rose 19% to $4.26 billion, and the shares rose 3.7%.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: The stock was down about 13% this year and roughly 25% below its February highs, so this is a beat against a very low bar. A 19% jump in operating profit on 5.6% revenue growth is a margin story, which means the pricing it took through the year is sticking.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: The Reserve Bank of India raised its repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% on Wednesday, its first hike since February 2023, and changed its stance to calibrated tightening.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: The rate decision was unanimous, but the stance change was 4 to 2, and that split is the interesting part. Two members wanted to keep the language neutral. The bank lifted its inflation forecast for this fiscal year to 5.2% from 5.0%, and it still sees growth of 7.1%.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: The risks it named were crude near $100 and a weak monsoon, and the rupee is around 96.4 to the dollar. India imports most of its oil, so an Iran premium in Brent goes straight into the central bank's reaction function.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: The Bank of England's governor Andrew Bailey said governments must rebuild confidence in public finances, with UK medium-term borrowing costs at a 19-year high. The ECB also published its account of the September 9 to 10 meeting, where it raised rates by 25 basis points, and its next decision is October 29.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: Put the 3 together. Delhi, London and Frankfurt are all fighting an energy-led inflation with a growth wobble underneath, and fiscal credibility is the variable bond markets keep testing.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: The one move on the tape that clears the bar is oil. Brent settled up 4.1% at about $104.28 on Thursday, driven by the Gulf shipping attacks, a hurricane threat to US offshore production, and a reported suspension of Chinese fuel exports. The International Energy Agency agreed to speed up its stock release and prioritize diesel.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: Equities were a story about tech rather than a broad sell-off. The Dow edged up while the Nasdaq fell on the OpenAI revenue question, and the S&P 500 sits a little below the record close it set on Tuesday. The full levels are in the Markets tab.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: What I would watch is the interaction between oil and rates. The 10-year Treasury yield was 5.28% on Wednesday by the Federal Reserve's own data, and it touched what looked like a multi-decade high on Thursday before easing. Those are long yields that already price a Fed that is not finished.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: St. Louis Fed president Musalem said the horizon for more hikes could stretch 6 to 9 months. The next FOMC meeting is October 28, with a hold the base case and a December hike still live, according to CME pricing. Weekly jobless claims came in at 197,000, so the labor market gives the Fed no reason to blink.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: That is the opinion piece: oil is acting as a tax on the consumer, rates are acting as a tax on the AI build-out, and the equity market has noticed the second one only this week.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: Agreed, and note the asymmetry. A de-escalation headline can knock $4 off Brent in a morning. Nothing comparable exists for a 5% long bond.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: Today's deep dive starts from a chart. The World Intellectual Property Organization released its 2026 Global Innovation Index on September 29, and the Economist's daily briefing this week framed the question around it: will Trump hurt America's ranking? We only have the Economist's headlines and framing from the newsletter, so the numbers here come from WIPO and open reporting, not from the article itself.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: The headline result is stability. Across 139 economies the top 5 are Switzerland, Sweden, the United States, South Korea and Singapore. Switzerland is first for the 16th straight year, and the US is third, unchanged. China is 10th, the only middle-income economy in the top 10, with Japan 12th and Hong Kong 14th.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: So on its face, no damage. And that is precisely the thesis worth chewing on. The index is built largely from stock and lagged data, patents already filed, papers already published, researchers already trained. It cannot yet register a funding shock that is only a couple of budget cycles old.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: Here is what the funding data says. The administration's fiscal 2026 request sought roughly 57% off the National Science Foundation and more than 40% off the National Institutes of Health. Congress largely rejected that. NIH ended up at $48.7 billion, up $415 million, and NSF down 3.4%. The fiscal 2027 request again proposes a 54% NSF cut, but that is a proposal, not law.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: Congress held the appropriations line, but execution is different from appropriation. NIH issued 12,588 grants in 2025, against a 2015 to 2024 average of 16,099. About $1.7 billion was reported withheld, and more than 2,200 grants worth $3.8 billion were cancelled. Reporting in Nature, which we have only second-hand, puts new NSF grants 25% below the 10-year average.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: That is the mechanism. You can keep the topline and still starve the pipeline, because the unit of science is the grant, and a grant that is never awarded never shows up as a cut. It shows up years later as a missing cohort of papers.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: Francis Collins, the former NIH director, put it as "this is a generation that we might lose," which is a claim about people rather than dollars. And the Economist has run a piece warning that America risks an academic brain drain. I should be clear that the hard emigration counts are not there yet. The evidence for the brain drain is largely anecdotal so far.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: The defenders have a real argument and it should be stated fairly. Their case is that NIH had grown too big and unfocused, that concentrating funds on fewer, higher-quality bets is a legitimate reform, and that the courts and Congress blocked the most indiscriminate cuts. Nothing in the index contradicts that.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: The index also shows a competitor's side of the story. The Shenzhen, Hong Kong, Guangzhou cluster is first for a 2nd year running, ahead of Tokyo-Yokohama, then San Jose and San Francisco, Beijing and Seoul. China has 25 clusters, one more than last year, and China and the US have led the cluster count for 4 years in a row.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: The new part of this year's report is a Dealroom and WIPO tracker of deep-science startups, companies built on university research. There are more than 30,000 of them, worth about $7.6 trillion, up 23% from 2024, and about $122 billion of venture capital went in during 2025. Half hold patents, against 15.4% of other startups.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: And the geography is lopsided. The US has 12,752 of those companies, China 3,466, the UK 2,133 and India 453. Central and Southern Asia grew 118% between 2020 and 2025, which is a growth rate from a small base but a direction worth noting.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: Those 12,752 companies are the answer to the question of why the US still ranks third. They are downstream of decades of federal basic research. An American University study models a 25% cut in public research funding as reducing GDP by 3.8% over the long run. That is a scenario, not a forecast, but it gives you the order of magnitude.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: Why should this listener care? Because the same logic applies to your sector. Advanced geothermal, small modular reactors, grid-scale storage chemistry, high-voltage equipment, these are all downstream of the federal science budget with a 10 to 15 year lag. The investments you are financing this decade are products of grants made in the 2010s.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: So the second-order read is about measurement. A rank that lags can stay high while the thing it measures erodes, and by the time it moves, the cause is a decade old and nobody can reverse it in a budget cycle. The question to ask of any index is not what it shows, but what it cannot yet see.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: I would add the Economist's own framing, that this administration is at once championing AI and waging what they call a war on science. Both can be true, and the headline rank can stay high because AI investment is private and enormous, while the public base that trains the people erodes quietly.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: That is the one to watch in the next edition. If the US slips, it will not be because of anything that happened this year.

segments.raw: SEGMENT FOUR — ENERGY / DATA CENTERS / UTILITIES
segments.label: Energy / Data Centers / Utilities

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: The Department of Energy filed a statement of position at FERC on October 7, its first FERC filing in at least 5 years. It says large loads must fund the generation they require, under what it calls a Ratepayer Protection Pledge, and it urges PJM to adopt the cost-allocation fixes FERC has already identified.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: This is the federal executive taking a side on cost causation. PJM's original July 31 filing targeted a 6.8 gigawatt shortfall with a price cap of $555 per megawatt-day, compared with $325 in the last base auction. The revised filing is due October 29, and there is a special Members Committee meeting on October 22.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: The market monitor's figure is the one that frames the politics. Data centers accounted for $6.3 billion, or 38%, of $16.4 billion in auction charges. That is a single-source number from the monitor, but it is the number legislators are using, and it explains why DOE would want its name on the ratepayer side.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: For a developer the implication is that bring-your-own-generation moves from a negotiating preference to a regulatory expectation. The spread between a load that arrives with its own capacity and one that arrives and leans on the market is about to be priced.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: A concrete price for firm capacity came out of Indiana. Hallador Power signed a 6-year contract with Duke Energy Indiana on October 7, per its 8-K, running June 1, 2029 to May 31, 2035. It is 200 megawatts of annual average base from the Merom coal plant, capacity plus energy, unit-contingent, and Duke can cut purchases to zero for up to 90 days per contract year.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: It is Hallador's 3rd capacity deal of 2026 and its highest capacity price yet, though the price is undisclosed. Latitude Media put the spring NIPSCO deal, 500 megawatts for 12 years at about $1 billion and serving Amazon and Google loads, at roughly $450 per megawatt-day. That works out to about $455 on the arithmetic, so treat it as an estimate, not a disclosed price.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: The read is that old coal is now a priced firm-capacity asset. No named data center is in this release, no regulatory approval is needed, and the forward book is $3 billion with a 460 megawatt gas project, Turtle Creek, in development. The unit-contingent language is the tell: Duke is buying availability, not a guarantee.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: Now the pledge versus permit pattern. Applied Digital announced on October 6 it has up to 1 gigawatt of potential power in Finland, its first non-US site, with initial power from 2028 and talks with hyperscalers under way.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: Look at what is missing. No named power counterparty, no signed tenant, no price, no initial megawatts, and further spend is contingent on customer demand and approvals. "Up to" 1 gigawatt is a site option. The distance between that and an energized hall is where most of the failures in this market live.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: One follow-on from the Midwest. MISO has proposed a fast-track study process for large loads paired with generation, and the one secondary summary I found puts it at a 120-day lane. I have no megawatt caps or filing date, so treat the 120 days as a single-source figure.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: If it holds, it is the same bargain DOE is pushing in PJM expressed as process: bring your own generation and you move to the front of the study line. The open question is whether 120 days survives contact with the actual network upgrades.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: The through-line from DOE to Hallador to Applied Digital is who carries the capacity risk. DOE says the load should. Hallador shows what firm power costs. Applied Digital shows how much of the market is still an option on power rather than power. For a developer, the diligence question is now which of the 3 you are underwriting.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: And it connects to the oil story we opened with. A reported suspension of Chinese fuel exports and a hurricane threat to Gulf of Mexico offshore output both fed Thursday's Brent move, which is a reminder that the fuel side of firm power is as exposed as the wires side.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: Magandang umaga. Dalawang salita ang pag-aaralan natin ngayong umaga na kaugnay ng balita sa Pilipinas. Ang una ay "pagsuko."

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: Ang "pagsuko" ay galing sa ugat na "suko." Ang karaniwang kahulugan nito ay ang pag-abot ng sarili sa kamay ng awtoridad, gaya ng isang akusadong humaharap sa korte o sa pulis. Sa balita, madalas mong maririnig na "hindi pa humaharap ang kongresista," at ang tanong ay kung kailan ang kaniyang pagsuko.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: Tama. Pero may ikalawang kahulugan din ang parehong ugat, ang pagtigil sa pakikibaka o pagtanggap ng pagkatalo. Kapag sinabi mong "sumuko na ako," puwede itong tungkol sa batas, puwede ring tungkol sa pagod. Kaya may bahid ito ng pagkatalo kahit sa opisyal na gamit.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: Ihambing mo ito sa "pagharap," na simpleng paglitaw sa harap ng korte o ng sinuman. Ang pagharap ay maaaring kusang-loob at walang kahihiyan. Ang pagsuko ay may kasamang pag-amin na wala nang takas, kaya mas mabigat ang dating.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: Halimbawa, "Hindi magkakaroon ng hurisdiksiyon ang korte hangga't walang pagsuko ang kongresista." Madalas itong sinusundan ng "sa" at ng awtoridad, gaya ng pagsuko sa pulisya, pagsuko sa NBI.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: Ang ikalawang salita ay "pagtutol." Ito ay ang pagsalungat o pagtanggi sa isang mungkahi, hakbang, o pahayag. Ito ang salitang ginagamit ng mga abogado kapag sinasabi nilang "may pagtutol po kami."

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: Pormal ang rehistro nito. Maririnig mo ito sa korte at sa Kongreso, at sa mga pahayag ng mga opisyal. Hindi ito karaniwan sa kuwentuhan sa bahay, kung saan mas madalas ang "ayoko" o "hindi ako sang-ayon."

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: Mas matatag din ang dating ng "pagtutol" kaysa sa simpleng hindi pagkakasundo. Ito ay tindig na may prinsipyo at may batayan. Kapag may pagtutol ang depensa, hinihingi nitong pagpasyahan ng hukom kung tama o mali ang tanong.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: Halimbawa, "Nagtaas ng pagtutol ang depensa sa tanong tungkol sa mga account sa ibang bansa." Kasingkahulugan nito ang "pagsalungat," pero ang pagsalungat ay mas malawak at kadalasang pampulitika.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: Para sa buod, ang "pagsuko" ay ang pag-abot sa awtoridad o ang pagtanggap ng pagkatalo, at ang "pagtutol" ay ang pormal na pagsalungat. Pareho mong maririnig sa susunod na bahagi, kaya pakinggang mabuti.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: Hinarang ng impeachment court noong Oktubre 7 ang pagtatangka ng prosekusyon na usisain ang BPI tungkol sa mga account ni Bise Presidente Sara Duterte sa ibang bansa, dahil sa batas sa lihim ng deposito sa bangko, at ito ay isang malinaw na pagtutol na umayon ang korte.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: Sa Senado, ang ika-37 araw ng paglilitis ay ginanap ngayong Oktubre 9, at hindi na magkakaroon ng paglilitis mula Oktubre 16 hanggang Nobyembre 8 dahil sa pagdinig sa badyet para sa 2027.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: Samantala, wala pa ring pagsuko si Batangas Representative Leandro Leviste, na umalis ng bansa noong Agosto 2, at ayon sa NBI, walang hurisdiksiyon ang korte hangga't hindi siya sumusuko o naaaresto.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: Let's stay in English for the rest. At the trial, the BIR's chief of staff Anne Loraine Garcia-Marquez testified and raised privacy concerns over revenue officers' details shown on screen, so the Senate took the livestream down. Presiding Officer Chiz Escudero called the unexplained-wealth charge "the meat of this article."

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: The new calendar matters politically. The spokesperson's projected December 16 verdict is disputed by Senator Raffy Tulfo, and a 3-week break for budget deliberations pushes the whole timetable. The trial and the 2027 budget are now competing for the same senators' time.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: On Leviste, the Public Service Act charge was filed by the DOJ over Solar Para Sa Bayan Corp. Two co-accused posted bail on October 7, arraignment is set for October 26, and the DOJ is said to be careful with process before tagging him a fugitive. The NBI is also looking at an alleged plot to frame Executive Secretary Ralph Recto, but I could not verify the details, so treat that as an open question.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: On the economy, the headline to carry into the weekend is that the BSP's next policy meeting is October 22, after the September inflation print of 7.2% that we covered yesterday. Anything that lifts oil, as Brent did on Thursday, narrows the central bank's room to wait.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: And a smaller item: the Inquirer's headline today has President Marcos framing the Pax Silica chip hub as a boost to the Philippines' role in the industry. I could not read the full article, so I will leave the specifics alone, but the July background was a 1,620 hectare area in New Clark City and job estimates ranging from 300,000 to 800,000, which tells you how soft the numbers still are.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: Tie it back to the through-line. In Manila, as in Washington and PJM, the interesting question is who carries the cost of a commitment, and the answer this week is that the courts and the calendar, not the principals, are setting the pace.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: Today's two Mandarin words come from the China story, and both are about consequence and time. The first is 于是, yúshì, a connective meaning "so" or "thereupon."

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: 于是 narrates what happened next, as a reaction. It sits in written register but is perfectly natural in speech. Here is an example. 房地产销售持续低迷，于是地方政府不得不重新考虑土地出让的节奏。 (Property sales stayed depressed, so local governments had to rethink the pace of land sales.)

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: The near-synonyms are 因此 and 所以, and the difference is worth knowing. 因此 and 所以 state a logical result, a cause and its conclusion. 于是 tells a story in sequence, so the result follows in time and is often an action someone chose.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: Right, so 所以 answers "why," while 于是 answers "and then what." Another example: 价格涨得太快，于是消费者开始观望。 (Prices rose too fast, and so consumers started to wait and see.) You would not swap 于是 for 所以 in a case where the second clause is not a reaction.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: The second word is 至今, zhìjīn, meaning "up to now" or "to this day." It is 书面语, written or formal register, and it most often pairs with 仍 or 没, to stress that a hoped-for change has not arrived.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: The spoken equivalent is 到现在. For example, 北京的刺激措施偏重供给，至今仍未见到能明显拉动居民消费的举措。 (Beijing's stimulus measures lean toward supply, and to this day there is no sign of a measure that clearly lifts household consumption.)

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: Another one: 这家公司至今没有公布具体的数字。 (The company still has not released specific figures.) The collocation to remember is 至今 plus 仍, 没, or 未.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: Both appear in the lead sentence of the China segment, so listen for them.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: 房地产销售持续低迷，于是北京推出了偏重供给的刺激措施，但至今仍未见到能明显拉动居民消费的举措。 (Property sales have stayed depressed, so Beijing rolled out supply-heavy stimulus measures, but to this day there is no sign of anything that clearly lifts household consumption.)

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: The setup is the package announced around September 30, ahead of the holiday. JPMorgan economists call it "state-guided and supply heavy." Bloomberg described it on October 2 as the biggest effort since September 2024, but "a nudge, not a game changer." The 2026 growth target is 4.5% to 5%.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: The next hard data is China's September CPI and PPI on October 14 at 9:30 in the morning Beijing time. I could not find a consensus, so I won't give you one. This is a preview, not a release.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: One more data point from this week's markets: a reported suspension of Chinese fuel exports helped push Brent up on Thursday. Bloomberg's October 8 newsletter framed the stimulus as something that may shore up GDP while reinforcing imbalances, though I have only the headline, not the text.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: And that is the two-speed read. Exports and industrial supply hold up on the outside. On the inside, the household and the local balance sheet are the weak links, and a supply-side package does not obviously fix either.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: Start at the Whitney, where "Roy Lichtenstein: Like New" has member previews this week and opens to the public on October 11, running to May 10, 2027. It has more than 130 works from the 1940s to the 1990s, organized by Meg Onli with guest curator Alex Da Corte, who has also made an outdoor version of the "Girl in Window" for the building.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: The detail I like is the reunion of the 8 works from Lichtenstein's 1962 Castelli debut, though one outlet disputes that the group is complete. There is also a 96-foot re-creation of the Greene Street Mural, the original of which was temporary and destroyed in 1988. It is billed as the first Whitney Lichtenstein retrospective since 1980.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: And the market side. Sotheby's Contemporary Curated sale on October 7 totaled $38.6 million, its highest ever for that format, with works chosen by NBA player Karl-Anthony Towns and Jordyn Woods, plus the late architect Robert A.M. Stern's collection, whose own sale runs through October 19.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: Labor is part of the Whitney story too. The museum's union ratified its contract on the eve of a strike during preview week, so the opening goes ahead on schedule. For an institution mounting a 130-work retrospective, that timing was not incidental.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: One more date for the calendar: the New Museum has named the 36 artists and collectives of its 2027 Triennial, drawn from 34 nations. Triennials are where curators place their bets, and a list that wide suggests the show is built around dispersal rather than a single center.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: In New York's institutional news, MoMA has staged a pop-up Epstein files reading room aimed at trustee Leon Black, according to The Art Newspaper on October 7. It is a protest-as-installation, and it keeps the question of who sits on museum boards in the news.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: Christie's October 1 postwar and contemporary sale made $28 million, 86% of its aggregate low estimate, and Judy Chicago's "Pasadena Lifesavers Blue Series #5" sold for $486,400, an artist record. Records for women artists keep arriving in the sales that are otherwise soft. The contrast says something: the curated, taste-led format is outperforming the traditional evening-sale model in a nervous market.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: Ian Bremmer, in Project Syndicate, argues the world has passed peak Trump. As the piece is framed, the President's ability to disrupt the international order has peaked, approval is falling, and foreign leaders who will outlast him are starting to write him off. AI is the exception he carves out.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: That is the steelman, and it has force: leaders hedge before they are certain. The counter is our own, not Bremmer's. Allies hedging is not the same as his leverage ending, because tariff and sanction tools run through executive authority, and a lame duck can still do real damage in the time left. Note we only have the gist of the piece, not the full text.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: Second, Andy Mukherjee in Bloomberg Opinion, on October 7: "AI Is Eating Software and Investors Have Noticed." He applies Solow's 1987 line, that computers are everywhere except the productivity statistics, to generative AI, in the context of the software-stock sell-off earlier this year.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: The steelman is that markets are pricing disruption before the revenue loss appears. Our counter-take is that incumbents with distribution and data can bundle AI as a feature, and that a story about software eaten by AI sits awkwardly beside this morning's story about the AI companies' own revenue being overstated.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: That is the irony of the week. The same market that punished software for being disrupted just punished the disruptor for its revenue accounting.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: In Phoenix, a 12-year-old named Sloan has delivered about 30,000 diapers to Nourish Phoenix, the food bank on 9th Avenue. When she was 7, she saw bare diaper shelves there and started a drive that collected about 7,000.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: This was her 5th annual drive. She aimed for 22,500, delivered about 30,000 in a U-Haul, and it was the food bank's largest diaper donation ever. She said, "If we have the ability to give people something that they might not have or need, it's really important to do that."

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: An empty shelf, a small idea, 5 years, and a record haul.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: That is The Morning Commute for Friday, October 9th. Thank you for listening, and have a good weekend.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: We will see you Monday.
